premises.statement: Over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially real-valued field, a smooth proper connected algebraic curve admits semistable vertex sets adapted to finitely many classical marks and finite type-II sets. Their actual canonical-affinoid formal models have the original analytic generic fibre, flat topologically finitely presented charts, proper reduced nodal residue fibre, and compatible refinement maps. Self-loops can be subdivided without deleting cycles.
premises.literal_version: literal arXiv1404.0279v1

premises.statement: For the same curve, the directed system of finite semistable skeleta has compatible retractions, covers all type-II/III points, and has inverse limit homeomorphic to the entire proper analytic curve. Rational functions with marked divisors satisfy the stated skeletal factorization and outgoing residual-order slope formula.
premises.literal_version: literal arXiv1404.0279v1

premises.statement: For adic rings/formal morphisms in the finite-ideal-type setting, formal etaleness is equivalent to etaleness of every compatible defining-ideal reduction, as in I.5.3.10–11. This applies to actual formal-etale charts over a complete principal-adic rank-one valuation ring.
premises.literal_version: literal Fujiwara-Kato2017v5; DISTINCT fromFreitag-Kiehl1988

premises.statement: Etale morphisms are stable under base change, are locally of finite presentation and flat, and an etale scheme over an algebraically closed field is a disjoint union of rational reduced points; an affine finitely presented fibre is finite.
premises.literal_version: Complete original Stacks HTML and text frozen20261007; immediate source, not a grant

premises.statement: A section of an unramified morphism is an open immersion; for a separated unramified morphism it is also a closed immersion. These assertions are obtained by base change of the diagonal.
premises.literal_version: Complete original Stacks HTML and text frozen20261007; immediate source, not a grant

premises.statement: In a Cartesian morphism of arbitrary thickenings of schemes, with both induced morphisms locally of finite type, properness of one induced morphism is equivalent to properness of the other. An arbitrary nil ideal need not have a uniform nilpotence exponent.
premises.literal_version: Complete original Stacks HTML and text frozen20261007; immediate source, not a grant

premises.statement: For a proper scheme of dimension at most one over a field, an invertible sheaf is ample if and only if its degree is strictly positive on every one-dimensional irreducible component. The proof uses the integral-curve degree criterion and a finite surjective cover by components and isolated points.
premises.literal_version: Original Stacks HTML/exact extracted text20261007

premises.statement: For an arbitrary proper morphism of schemes and an invertible sheaf, ampleness on one fibre implies relative ampleness over an open neighbourhood of that base point. The proof passes to finite-type integer stages before using a Noetherian fibre theorem.
premises.literal_version: Original Stacks HTML/exact extracted text20261007

premises.statement: For a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps, finitely presented schemes over the limit descend to a stage; morphisms and eventual equality descend. The finite affine presentations, overlap maps and cocycle identities all descend.
premises.literal_version: Complete original Stacks HTML and text frozen20261007; immediate source, not a grant

premises.statement: An invertible sheaf on the limit of a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transitions descends as an invertible sheaf. An inverse sheaf and the evaluation isomorphism can be descended together at a common later stage.
premises.literal_version: Complete original Stacks HTML and text frozen20261007; immediate source, not a grant

premises.statement: For a morphism between finitely presented schemes over such an inverse system, local finite type at an initial stage and properness at the limit imply properness at some later stage.
premises.literal_version: Complete original Stacks HTML and text frozen20261007; immediate source, not a grant

premises.statement: For a locally finitely presented morphism between finitely presented schemes over such an inverse system, flatness at the limit implies flatness at a later stage.
premises.literal_version: Complete original Stacks HTML and text frozen20261007; immediate source, not a grant

premises.statement: An invertible sheaf at an initial stage whose pullback to a quasi-compact quasi-separated inverse limit with affine transitions is ample becomes ample at a later stage. A finite cover by nonvanishing sections of positive powers may first be raised to a common power without changing its loci.
premises.literal_version: Complete original Stacks HTML and text frozen20261007; immediate source, not a grant

premises.statement: On a quasi-compact scheme with ample invertible sheaf, every finite-type quasi-coherent sheaf tensored by all sufficiently high powers is generated by finitely many global sections. The stated ample equivalences and generation implication are those of 28.27.13.
premises.literal_version: Complete original Stacks HTML and text frozen20261007; immediate source, not a grant

premises.statement: For a proper scheme over a Noetherian ring, an ample invertible sheaf and a coherent sheaf, coherent cohomology modules are finite and all higher cohomology of sufficiently high twists vanishes. Only a finite range of cohomological degrees is needed for a bounded affine Cech cover.
premises.literal_version: Complete original Stacks HTML and text frozen20261007; immediate source, not a grant

premises.statement: Raynaud–Gruson 3.4.6: for a locally finitely presented morphism X to S and a finite-type module M, if the weak assassin of S is locally finite, the S-flat locus of M is open and M is finitely presented there. Flatness is over S, not over a polynomial ring presenting X.
premises.literal_version: Original publisher PDF/extracted text; RG ordinary extraction has NOarticletext

premises.statement: A complete valuation ring for a nonzero principal adic topology, and its topologically finitely generated algebras, lie in the topologically universally adhesive scope of 0.9.2.7 and I.2.1.4(2). In the rank-one proof, a torsion-free finite restricted-series module is valuation-ring flat and its reduction is flat over the quotient base.
premises.literal_version: literal Fujiwara-Kato2017v5; DISTINCT fromFreitag-Kiehl1988

premises.statement: In the printed topologically universally adhesive case, for a proper morphism of separated finite-type schemes over U=Spec(A) minus the adic closed locus, coherent higher direct images commute with rigid analytification. In degree zero this identifies global algebraic and analytic sections of the same coherent sheaf on an already algebraic proper scheme.
premises.literal_version: literal Fujiwara-Kato2017v5; DISTINCT fromFreitag-Kiehl1988

premises.statement: For a good analytic space, coherent sheaves and their cohomology agree between the ordinary and analytic G-topology as in 1.3.4–6. Over a nontrivially valued field, a Hausdorff strict analytic space has the same rigid carrier and coherent sheaves under 1.6.1–2; the final comparison gives the same H0 on identical affinoid modules and cocycles.
premises.literal_version: Original publisher PDF/extracted text; RG ordinary extraction has NOarticletext

premises.statement: For the stated flat separated topologically finite-type formal models, the analytic germ reduction and a formal metrized bundle have the component-closure premodel in 6.5.1/6.6.8. On a good germ, analytic functions are dense in the completed residue field; reduced cocycles lift and residual-bundle isomorphisms give PL-metrized germ isomorphisms under 6.5.3–5 and 6.6.1–8.
premises.literal_version: Literal arxiv1204.6277v1,27April2012,124pages

premises.statement: For a locally trivial PL line bundle on a germ with dense analytic local functions in its completed residue field, generated residual bundle is equivalent to the specified minimum-of-unit-norm presentation. The complete local approachability and calibrated atomic calculation is 6.8.2–3 in its compact pure-dimensional domain.
premises.literal_version: Literal arxiv1204.6277v1,27April2012,124pages

premises.statement: In literal 1204.6277v1, a PL metrized bundle on a good separated pure curve has atomic curvature in the full-definition-dimensional germs. For a generically smooth boundaryless curve over an algebraically closed complete field, the entire AC calibrated-cone proof gives each coefficient as the degree of the residual bundle on a proper whole-residue-field model. The value index is one. Linearity and the difference of generated residual bundles cover signed and zero degrees; lower-definition-dimensional germs have coefficient zero.
premises.literal_version: Literal arxiv1204.6277v1,27April2012,124pages

premises.statement: For projective geometrically reduced schemes over complete valued fields and semiample rational bundles, the actual weighted FS definition and closure laws apply. Every psh metric is smooth-semipositive regularizable; a continuous endpoint is uniformly so. The continuous mixed measure and signed dpsh calculus are the genuine smooth-approximation operators, with uniform-to-weak continuity and raw intersection mass.
premises.literal_version: literal arXiv1805.01016v3

premises.statement: For an algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued field and an actual semistable reduction of a smooth proper curve, BL85 2.4–2.5 identify the annular formal fibre and residual branch order. Whole 3.1–3.2 relate zeros/poles and the two component norms to that branch order, including an ordinary node whose two branches lie on the same component.

premises.statement: On a generalized annulus the negative logarithm of a meromorphic function is piecewise affine with integer slopes given by the Newton-polygon formula. On complementary balls a unit has constant norm; the complete 2.12–2.13 proof makes a unit norm factor through the annular retraction.
premises.literal_version: literal arXiv1404.0279v1

premises.statement: For a proper pure-dimensional algebraic variety and globally approachable line-bundle metrics, the total curvature mass is the raw intersection degree. Whole 6.4.3–5 explicitly requires global approachability; local approachability alone is not asserted to imply this mass formula.

On the smooth residual locus of the actual node chart one coordinate is invertible, leaving an etale chart over a localized affine line. A C-point lying in the formal generic chart evaluates powerbounded functions in R. In the finite residual fibre, a principal function can be one at the chosen rational root and zero at all other roots. Completing that norm-one localization preserves the actual evaluation and deletes the other roots.

On xy=b, x and y are regular meromorphic elements by flatness and b nonzero. The factors cv*x^m compare to cv and cw by x^m and (cv*b^m/cw)*y^-m. The exact endpoint forces the scalar ratio to have norm one, hence it and its inverse are integral. No ratio need literally equal one. In frame f^-1 the canonical generic section is f times that frame, so its weight is -log|f|. The residual transition ev=x^m*ee has divisor order +m at the v branch and -m at the other branch. Thus the degree is N*Delta_out g with the printed sign.

actual_application_hypothesis_and_domain: On the smooth residual locus of the actual node chart one coordinate is invertible, leaving an etale chart over a localized affine line. A C-point lying in the formal generic chart evaluates powerbounded functions in R. In the finite residual fibre, a principal function can be one at the chosen rational root and zero at all other roots. Completing that norm-one localization preserves the actual evaluation and deletes the other roots.

FK supplies etaleness of every reduction. The zero fibre Qj is affine etale over Rj. Its extended nil ideal is nil because each individual sum uses finitely many nil coefficients; hence its only prime lies over the one remaining residual point. Its evaluation section is an open and closed immersion by the etale diagonal. An open immersion meeting that sole point covers the entire scheme, including its structure sheaf.

Monicity of t-c proves regularity even over a nonreduced base; etale flatness preserves it. The evaluation-zero h has a unique quotient modulo each power. Uniqueness forces compatibility and completeness gives the actual quotient in B. Separation also proves regularity in B. The ideal is exactly the closed evaluation kernel, so its generic quotient is the original C-point and its residue quotient has length one. On overlaps equality of these regular principal ideals gives unit ratios; outside the residual mark nilness followed by geometric inversion gives a unit. This proves the actual horizontal Cartier divisor without a completion-ideal inference.

actual_application_hypothesis_and_domain: Each edge contributes -(hw-hv)^2/ell to sum h*Delta_out h; both incidences of a loop cancel for vertex-affine values. Connectedness gives constant kernel and hence zero-sum image for the symmetric matrix. Q-A has zero sum. With one edgeless vertex the original horizontal degree is already positive. The proof does not replace the cyclic graph by a tree.

Approximate one shared height per vertex. Each edge length and endpoint difference belong to Gamma, and rational division preserves Gamma. Rational p<s<q give t=(q*ell-difference)/(q-p) strictly inside the edge and the exact endpoint. New outgoing curvature is q-p>0. Finite valence makes the old errors smaller than Q*/4; both loop incidences are included. Uniform height/slope errors tend to zero. No subsequent zero-degree vertex is introduced into a purported positive final pair.

On xy=b, x and y are regular meromorphic elements by flatness and b nonzero. The factors cv*x^m compare to cv and cw by x^m and (cv*b^m/cw)*y^-m. The exact endpoint forces the scalar ratio to have norm one, hence it and its inverse are integral. No ratio need literally equal one. In frame f^-1 the canonical generic section is f times that frame, so its weight is -log|f|. The residual transition ev=x^m*ee has divisor order +m at the v branch and -m at the other branch. Thus the degree is N*Delta_out g with the printed sign.

Horizontal tensor power plus the signed vertical divisor preserves the generic dNL and gives positive degrees on all final components, summing Nda by incidence cancellation. A scalar perturbation h of a DL reference requires vertical weight DN*h. All later section powers multiply D*N, rather than clearing only graph slopes. Local frames of rational bundles are interpreted on these cleared integral powers.
